$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.

Link lifecycle: LinkProvider starts the controller with onNetwork (expo-network) and onForeground (AppState change, calls cb only when state is active). No background branch, no close on background, no foreground service, no background task module in package.json.

Keep-alive is JS setTimeout: schedulePing every PING_EVERY_MS (25s); pong timer PONG_WITHIN_MS (15s) closes the conn and calls dropped(Closed). Backgrounding stalls these timers; the socket is reassessed only on the next active state (ping if live, else attempt).

Inbox events: onHost handles inbox-updated and snapshot by calling reconcileAll and flush. The reducer replaces one session items (filter out the touched session_ids, keep the rest). An empty payload is a no-op.
Session status arrives as event session-updated (upsert into data.sessions). A snapshot message replaces all data.

Diff point for new item appeared: in onHost, this.state.data.inbox is the previous set; the reduce result from apply() (controller.ts:425-429, which calls reduce(this.state.data, msg)) gives the new set. The snapshot also goes through this path, so an initial-connect guard is needed or every existing item would notify on connect.

A1 camera permission pattern: useCameraPermissions; a rationale screen (copy.rationale_title, rationale_body, rationale_button) shown before requestPermission; denied path shows denied_retry when canAskAgain, else denied_settings with Linking.openSettings().
No settings or about screen exists. Routes are mobile/src/app/_layout.tsx, index.tsx (home, with a forget action in a banner), pair.tsx and inbox/[id].tsx.

Inbox item route is /inbox/[id] with param id, pushed from home by router.push with pathname /inbox/[id] and params id. File: mobile/src/app/inbox/[id].tsx. Scheme orchestra gives orchestra://inbox/<id>.

Jest: package.json jest block uses preset jest-expo, moduleNameMapper for css and the @/ alias, testPathIgnorePatterns, and transformIgnorePatterns that allow @noble. No setupFiles. No jest.mock calls under src/__tests__. The only file in __mocks__ is style.js. expo-camera and expo-crypto are not mocked by hand; they rely on the jest-expo preset.

Protocol types: InboxItem {id, session_id, kind: permission|question|finished|error, created_at, resolved, expired, summary, tool_name, tool_input_preview, questions, result_text, host?}. SessionSummary {id, project_id, project_name, status, started_at, last_activity_at, ...}. SessionStatus includes waiting_permission, waiting_question, needs_attention, idle. Human-readable title: InboxItem.summary. Session context: SessionSummary.project_name.

architect.rationale: Single-loop. One app, one builder, three sequential slices on one branch of the orchestra git repo. Not a diamond: s1 owns package.json, package-lock.json and app.json (shared hotspots); s2 needs the installed expo-notifications from s1 for types and jest; s3 calls s2 notify/os.ts and notify/payload.ts. Every edge carries a real artifact, so it is a sequence, and the change fits one reviewable diff. Risk: s1 HIGH because it touches app.json (native config rule) and adds a native module plus config plugin, which changes the fingerprint runtimeVersion. s2 HIGH because it decides what text reaches the notification shade and lock screen (a test can assert data is only {id, kind} but cannot judge what a lock screen shows) and it edits controller.ts, the link core. s3 LOW: no sensitive data (the tap id is validated by s2 parseTap), no file shared with another slice, covered by jest plus owner checks. Owner decision, not reopened: local notifications only, while open or briefly backgrounded; no foreground service; no FCM, register_push or relay (PR3). The scout plan-killer (no background keep-alive) is accepted by that decision and stated in the rationale copy. Desktop, core and protocol untouched: snapshot and inbox-updated already carry everything needed. POST_NOTIFICATIONS is declared explicitly in app.json android.permissions (convention: declarations live in app.json; harmless if the library also declares it), and s1 proves it by prebuild plus a grep of the generated manifest. New build required: expo-notifications is a native module, so the fingerprint changes and it cannot ship OTA. No ops step in this run; the next EAS build is an ops follow-up. Local notifications work in Expo Go on Android (F7), so owner checks run in Expo Go.

design.fresh_rule: src/link/fresh.ts, pure. The controller keeps known = set of ids in the current inbox. On snapshot: known = ids(new inbox), notify nothing. On inbox-updated: fresh = items in the reduced inbox whose id is not in known, kind permission or question, not resolved, not expired; then known = ids(new inbox). Fires only when snapshotConn === conn, so an inbox-updated before this connection's snapshot notifies nothing. A reconnect or seq gap reseeds from the next snapshot, so items that arrived while disconnected are not notified (they show in Needs you). forget and revoke clear known. It also reports gone = previously notified ids no longer pending, so their notification is dismissed.
design.controller_hook: Deps gains optional onInbox(e: {fresh: InboxItem[], gone: string[]}), called from onHost after apply(). The controller never imports expo-notifications.
design.payload: src/notify/payload.ts, pure. content = title '<Kind> from <project>', body = summary cut to 100 chars with an ellipsis or the fallback, data = {id, kind}. Never tool_name, tool_input_preview, questions, result_text, host address, keys, answers or drafts. identifier = item id, so dismiss works and repeats collapse. parseTap(data) returns the id only if it is a non-empty string of at most 128 chars, else null.
design.os_adapter: src/notify/os.ts is the only importer of expo-notifications. ensureChannel() calls setNotificationChannelAsync('needs-you', name 'Needs you', importance HIGH, lockscreenVisibility PRIVATE). request() calls ensureChannel first, then requestPermissionsAsync. Also getStatus, post, dismiss, dismissAll, and setNotificationHandler (banner and list shown, sound on, no badge). In memory only; nothing is written to disk or logged.
design.suppress_rule: Do not post when AppState.currentState is 'active' AND the current route is '/' (home, where Needs you is shown) or '/inbox/<that id>'. Otherwise post: active on another screen (pair, a different item), or background or inactive. The root layout pushes the route into the notifier with usePathname.
design.tap: The listener goes in the root layout _layout.tsx, inside LinkProvider: addNotificationResponseReceivedListener for warm taps plus useLastNotificationResponse for a cold start. parseTap, then router.push to pathname /inbox/[id] with params id; invalid data goes to '/'. A tap for an item that has gone lands on the existing inbox/[id] gone state (copy.gone), so no new code is needed. A tap also dismisses that notification.
design.settings_surface: No settings screen. One compact Alerts card at the bottom of home (index.tsx), in components/alerts-card.tsx, shown only when paired. Undetermined: rationale title and body plus [Turn on alerts] [Not now]; Not now hides it for this app run only, in memory. Denied with canAskAgain: alerts_denied_retry. Denied without canAskAgain: alerts_denied_settings with Linking.openSettings(). Granted: the one-line alerts_on with [Notification settings], which calls Linking.openSettings(). Status is re-read on AppState active, after a return from Settings.
design.jest: Screen tests use jest.mock('@/notify/os'), a hand mock of our own adapter. payload and fresh are pure and need no mock. The adapter test relies on the jest-expo preset stub if one exists for expo-notifications, as expo-camera and expo-crypto do; otherwise one jest.mock('expo-notifications') goes in that single test file. No global setupFiles.

copy_for_approval.alerts_body: Orchestra can alert you when an agent asks for permission or has a question. Alerts only arrive while Orchestra is open or was used recently, and only while this phone is on the same network as your desktop, or on Tailscale. If the app is closed or the phone has been asleep for a while, no alert arrives.

copy_for_approval.alerts_denied_settings: Alerts are off. To get them, allow notifications for Orchestra in Settings. [Open settings]

s1.$comment: RE-REVIEWS NEST, and this is the rule every reader follows. The TOP LEVEL of reviews.<slice> IS attempt 1. A re-review writes attempt_2, then attempt_3, and so on, each with the same fields as the top level. Every attempt SURVIVES PERMANENTLY - history is never overwritten, flattened, or migrated up. The LATEST attempt supplies the verdict: that is what close-run.py, brief.py and verify-state.py resolve through, and what fleetview's finalVerdict() has always shown. `ever_rejected` - did ANY attempt REJECT - is DISPLAY ONLY, forever, so a rejection stays visible after it is fixed; it must never gate anything, or the fleet stops being able to loop. NO NODE MAY REWRITE AN EARLIER ATTEMPT: a second reviewer writes its own attempt_N and leaves the ones before it alone, top-level verdict included - relocating that verdict would destroy the history the board keeps and leave a key stamped written_by:reviewer with someone else as its real author. The KEY INDEX numbers an attempt, not the `attempt` field inside it; the field is display. An EMPTY attempt_N is not a re-review, it is a key nobody wrote - write the whole attempt or none of it. The walk STOPS AT THE FIRST GAP, so an attempt_3 with no attempt_2 is ignored and the earlier verdict stands: A GAP IS MALFORMED AND NO NODE MAY LEAVE ONE. Write the next UNUSED N and never skip - a mis-numbered re-review is not reported anywhere, it is simply unread, and a REJECT nobody reads is a REJECT nobody acts on. The cap is attempt_9, matching fleetview's `for (i = 2; i < 10; i++)` exactly so the two readers cannot disagree; attempt_10 and beyond is reported loudly and resolved by nobody.

s2.summary: PASS. Re-ran npm ci, jest (20 suites, 424 passed), tsc (exit 0) and the grep gate (only src/notify/os.ts) at dfbcbef; both commits njcurtis3, no trailers. Attempt 1's blocker is fixed: os.post() awaits ensureChannel() before scheduleNotificationAsync, and os.post is the only schedule path (notifier.ts:29), so the first post after a cold start with permission already granted lands on 'needs-you'. In expo-notifications 57.0.24, AndroidXNotificationsChannelManager applies lockscreenVisibility PRIVATE (enum 2 -> VISIBILITY_PRIVATE); re-creating an existing channel is an Android no-op except name and description, so it is idempotent. If setNotificationChannelAsync rejects, the await throws, nothing is scheduled and the notifier swallows it: it fails closed, never posts on the fallback channel. On API 24-25 there are no channels and the Notification default visibility is PRIVATE. The body is now cut at 100 code points (up to 200 UTF-16 units); the approved copy says '100 chars', which code points honour. Fix touched only os.ts and payload.ts, so the snapshot guard, {id,kind} data and the suppress rule are unchanged.

findings.detail: ensureChannel passes no showBadge, so the channel gets the Android default (NotificationChannel showBadge=true; expo only calls setShowBadge when the key is present, AndroidXNotificationsChannelManager.java:122-124). Result: a launcher dot, with no content and no count. The design's 'no badge' is about the handler's shouldSetBadge:false, which is set, and not_doing excludes badge work, so this is not a contract breach. If the owner wants no dot, add showBadge:false before first ship, because channel settings freeze once the channel exists.

If channel creation fails, the alert is silently dropped: the await throws before schedule and notifier.swallow eats it. Failing closed is the right trade, since the alternative is the fallback channel with a public lock screen, and the design forbids logging. On iOS every post calls the stub setNotificationChannelAsync, which writes a constant console.debug line with no content. iOS is out of scope.

BODY_MAX counts code points (Array.from), so a cut body is 99 code points plus the ellipsis, at most 100 code points, which can be up to about 200 UTF-16 units. The approved copy ('at most 100 chars') is user-visible characters, so code points fit better than units, and nothing downstream caps on UTF-16 length. ZWJ sequences and flag pairs can still be split between code points. That renders as separate glyphs, not a lone surrogate. Cosmetic.

s3.summary: PASS. Attempt 1's blocker is fixed. onTap now clears the stored response before it routes, so a root remount in the same runtime reads null. A cold-start tap is still routed exactly once: it is read, cleared, then the listener subscribes. I traced this through expo-notifications 57.0.24. getLastNotificationResponseAsync is literally async wrapping the sync call, so the sync version can never return null where the old one would not. On both Android (NotificationManager pending extras) and iOS (NotificationCenterManager pendingResponses), the native module replays the launch tap into lastResponse inside its own OnCreate, which runs before any JS call into the module returns. tapRoute/parseTap send non-objects, a missing, empty or non-string id, or one over 128 characters home. The os.ts s2 guarantees still hold, and it is the only non-test importer. Card, copy and index are unchanged since attempt 1; the copy still matches word for word. I re-ran npm ci, tsc (exit 0), jest (22 suites, 437 tests), the copy grep (3) and authorship (njcurtis3, no trailers). Notes: a narrow double-route race, the web throw, and NotifyBridge still has no test.

findings.issue: Narrow double-route race. Native sets lastResponse and then queues the JS event. If that lands while the effect runs, after native set it but before JS dispatches the event, takeLaunchTap routes and clears, and then the newly subscribed onTap fires on the queued event and pushes the same item again. The window is only during mount (the same window useLastNotificationResponse dedupes by request.identifier), and attempt 1's async version had it too. A fix: remember the last handled request.identifier in os.ts and skip repeats.

On web, NotificationsEmitterModule has no getLastNotificationResponse, so the sync call throws UnavailabilityError synchronously inside NotifyBridge's effect. That crashes the root under `npm run web`. Before, the async version rejected and the rejection was swallowed. Web is not a target (registry ui is native-desktop + native-mobile), so this is a note only.

NotifyBridge still has no test. The once-only and remount guarantees are proven only at the os.ts level, using a mock whose clear nulls mockLast. Nothing renders the bridge twice to show it does not re-route.
Carried from attempt 1: a cold-start tap can show the gone copy briefly before the link snapshot arrives.

attempt_1.summary: REJECT on one os.ts bug. A warm tap is never cleared: onTap only routes, and the native emitter stores every tap as lastNotificationResponse (NotificationsEmitter.kt:78). takeLaunchTap clears only on cold start. So when the root remounts in the same JS runtime, NotifyBridge's effect runs again and re-routes to an old item. That happens when the activity is recreated after a font-scale or locale change (Expo's configChanges leave both out), or on Android 11 and older after Back exits and the app is reopened. The fix is one line: clear the last response in onTap too. Everything else holds. os.ts is still the only importer. The API names match the 57.0.24 .d.ts. The listener unsubscribes. ensureChannel still runs before post and request, PRIVATE is kept, and showBadge is false. Route tracking feeds '/' and '/inbox/<id>' to isSuppressed, and nothing races a pair redirect. The card copy matches copy_for_approval word for word, and the card shows only when link.host is set. Touchable adds role and the 48dp clamp. I re-ran npm ci, tsc (exit 0), jest (22 suites, 435 tests), the copy grep (3) and authorship (njcurtis3, no trailers). The risk tag should be medium, not low.

findings.issue: A warm tap stays stored and is re-routed when the root remounts.
findings.evidence: NotificationsEmitter.kt:70-79 sets lastNotificationResponseBundle on every response, warm taps included, and only clearLastNotificationResponse resets it. onTap never clears it. NotifyBridge runs takeLaunchTap() every time it mounts. Repro: with the app backgrounded, tap the notification for item X. onTap pushes /inbox/X, and last stays X. Then change the system font size (fontScale is not in Expo's configChanges 'keyboard|keyboardHidden|orientation|screenSize|screenLayout|uiMode|smallestScreenSize'), so the activity is recreated. RN unmounts and remounts the root in the same JS runtime. takeLaunchTap returns X and router.push('/inbox/X') runs again, so the user lands on a stale item or the gone screen. Android 11 and older does the same after Back on home and a relaunch. The comment 'Cleared so it is handled once' is true only for cold start.
findings.fix: In onTap, call Notifications.clearLastNotificationResponse() before cb (or have open() clear). Add an os.test case: after a warm tap, takeLaunchTap() returns null.

The design said 'no new code is needed' for the gone state, but did not cover the window before connect. O7 should look for this flash.
